stem: A company runs a latency-sensitive application in AWS account A and its database in AWS account B, in the us-east-1 Region. Both accounts were created in 2021. The VPCs of the two accounts are connected, and each account creates subnets in its own VPC. The company wants the application instances and the database in the same physical Availability Zone. The engineers in each account choose zones by the names that their own console shows, such as us-east-1a. The company must ensure that both workloads use the same physical zone. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: choose zones by the names that their own console shows
ensure that both workloads use the same physical zone

options.text: Create the application subnet in the zone that has the same Availability Zone name, such as us-east-1a, as the database subnet in the other account.
options.why: For accounts created before November 2025, a zone name [might not be the same physical location as it is in another account](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-az-name-mapping-independent-per-account), so matching names does not ensure one physical zone.
options.misconception: An Availability Zone name such as us-east-1a is the same physical zone in every account.

options.text: Move the application and the database into one AWS account, so that both workloads see the same zone names for the same physical zones.
options.why: It can work, but moving a workload between accounts is far more work than reading one zone attribute in each account.

options.text: Open an AWS Support case to ask AWS to map the Availability Zone names of both accounts to the same physical zones.
options.why: No support case is needed, because an AZ ID already names [the same physical location in every AWS account](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-az-id-same-physical-location-every-account).
options.misconception: AWS Support remaps the zone names of an account on request.

options.text: Look up the AZ ID of the database subnet, such as use1-az2, and create the application subnet in the zone with the same AZ ID.
options.why: An AZ ID names [the same physical location in every AWS account](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-az-id-same-physical-location-every-account), so equal AZ IDs mean one physical zone.

explanation: An Availability Zone ID (AZ ID) names [the same physical location in every AWS account](../facts/global-infrastructure.md#global-infrastructure-az-id-same-physical-location-every-account). Each team looks up the AZ ID of the database zone and creates its subnet in the zone with the matching AZ ID. This needs no move between accounts and no support case.
takeaway: Across accounts, match Availability Zones by AZ ID, not by zone name.
twin: If the stem said "both workloads run in one AWS account" instead: the zone name is enough, because one account sees one physical zone behind each of its zone names.
say: Across accounts I'd match zones by AZ ID, because the AZ ID is the same physical zone everywhere.
